item.title: Windows 11 October Update Cripples Developer Tools: Localhost Connections Mysteriously Fail
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: Microsoft resolved a critical Windows 11 bug that broke localhost connections (127.0.0.1) over HTTP/2 protocols, affecting developers and enterprise applications. The issue, introduced by October updates KB5066835 and KB5065789, prevented Visual Studio debugging, SQL Server Management Studio authentication, and other critical applications from functioning properly. Microsoft fixed the problem through a Known Issue Rollback (KIR) update, which users can install via Windows Update followed by a system restart to restore localhost functionality.
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft Fixes Critical Windows 11 Bug That Broke Localhost Connections **Update October 17, 2025:** Microsoft has resolved the issue through a Known Issue Rollback (KIR) update, with additional details provided below. Microsoft’s October Windows 11 updates introduced a significant bug that disabled localhost functionality, preventing applications from connecting to the local IP address 127.0.0.

item.title: 266,000+ F5 BIG-IP Systems Left Vulnerable After Nation-State Hackers Steal Critical Security Flaws
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: A major cybersecurity breach at F5 Networks has exposed over 266,000 BIG-IP devices worldwide to potential attacks. Chinese nation-state hackers from group UNC5291 infiltrated F5's network for at least a year, stealing source code and vulnerability information while deploying Brickstorm malware. F5 has released patches for 44 vulnerabilities, and CISA issued emergency directives requiring federal agencies to update systems by October 31. The breach is particularly concerning as compromised F5 devices can provide attackers with network access, credential theft capabilities, and persistent backdoors into critical infrastructure systems.

item.title: Microsoft Patches “Highest Ever” Severity Flaw That Could Hijack User Credentials in ASP.NET Core
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: Microsoft has patched a critical ASP.NET Core vulnerability (CVE-2025-55315) affecting the Kestrel web server with the platform's highest-ever severity rating. This HTTP request smuggling flaw allows authenticated attackers to hijack credentials, bypass security controls, access sensitive data, modify server files, and crash servers. Microsoft urges immediate updates for all ASP.NET Core users across .NET 8+, .NET 2.3, and self-contained applications, with specific installation instructions for each version. The fix was part of January's Patch Tuesday addressing 172 total security flaws, making this a high-priority update for organizations running ASP.NET Core applications.

item.title: Europol Crushes Massive SIM-Box Empire That Fueled 3,200 Fraud Cases and €4.5M in Losses
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: European law enforcement dismantled a massive SIM-box fraud network in Operation SIMCARTEL, shutting down illegal services operating through gogetsms.com and apisim.com. The criminal enterprise used 1,200 SIM-box devices with 40,000 SIM cards from 80+ countries to generate 49 million fraudulent online accounts, facilitating over 3,200 fraud cases including phishing, investment scams, and police impersonation schemes. Coordinated raids across Austria, Estonia, Finland, and Latvia resulted in seven arrests and seizure of criminal infrastructure, €431,000 in frozen accounts, $333,000 in cryptocurrency, and luxury vehicles. The operation caused millions in damages, with Austria reporting €4.5 million and Latvia €420,000 in losses.

item.title: Microsoft Clears Path for Windows 11 24H2: Two Major Update Blocks Removed After Critical Fixes
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: Microsoft has removed two compatibility blocks preventing Windows 11 24H2 upgrades, resolving issues with enterprise security software using SenseShield Technology drivers that caused system crashes, and wallpaper applications that created desktop display problems. The company previously lifted restrictions related to camera functionality and Bluetooth audio issues. Additionally, Windows 11 25H2 (2025 Update) is now available for users with early update settings enabled, while Home and Pro users receive automatic updates with postponement options.

item.title: North Korean Hackers Weaponize Blockchain to Deploy Evolved Malware Arsenal in Stealth Attacks
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: North Korean hackers behind the "Contagious Interview" campaign are evolving their malware arsenal by merging BeaverTail and OtterCookie capabilities and pioneering the use of blockchain networks as command-and-control servers. The group targets job seekers through fake recruitment scams, deploying sophisticated malware with enhanced keylogging, screenshot capture, cryptocurrency theft, and remote access capabilities. Recent attacks involved malicious Node.js applications and compromised npm packages, demonstrating the threat actors' continued innovation in social engineering tactics and technical sophistication to evade detection while maximizing data theft impact.

item.title: North Korean Hackers Deploy Sophisticated AkdoorTea Backdoor in Massive Crypto Developer Infiltration Campaign
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: North Korean hackers are conducting a sophisticated multi-platform cyber campaign called "Contagious Interview," targeting software developers worldwide with advanced malware including the newly discovered AkdoorTea backdoor. The attackers pose as recruiters on job platforms like LinkedIn and Upwork, using fake video assessments and malicious coding exercises to deploy malware across Windows, Linux, and macOS systems. The campaign specifically targets cryptocurrency and Web3 developers, utilizing tools like BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, and the advanced TsunamiKit for data theft and system persistence. This operation connects to North Korea's broader fraudulent IT worker scheme, combining traditional identity theft with advanced cyber operations to infiltrate legitimate companies using stolen identities.

item.title: DDoS Attacks Surge 41% as Hackers Unleash Record-Breaking 2.2 Tbps Assault on Tech Companies
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: DDoS attacks surged 41% year-over-year with a record-breaking 2.2 Tbps assault, while attack frequency jumped 21% to 1.17 million incidents in H1 2025. The technology sector now faces 30% of all attacks, overtaking gaming as the primary target, followed by financial services at 21%. Cybercriminals are deploying more sophisticated multi-vector strategies with longer durations and application-layer attacks rising to 38% of incidents. Factors driving this escalation include accessible DDoS-for-hire services, IoT vulnerabilities, geopolitical tensions, and advanced attack techniques targeting business logic flaws in e-commerce and payment systems.

item.title: Hackers Infiltrate Rust Package Registry: 8,400+ Downloads of Fake Crates Designed to Steal Crypto Wallet Keys
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers discovered a sophisticated supply chain attack targeting cryptocurrency developers through malicious Rust packages. Two fake libraries—faster_log and async_println—impersonated the legitimate fast_log library, accumulating over 8,400 downloads before detection. The packages used typosquatting tactics, copied original documentation for cover, and embedded code to scan for Ethereum and Solana private keys in source files, transmitting stolen wallet credentials to command-and-control servers. The malicious packages were removed from crates.io following responsible disclosure, but the incident highlights critical supply chain security risks in cryptocurrency development where stolen private keys can cause immediate financial losses.
item.content:encoded:

Two fake libraries designed to steal digital wallet credentials were recently discovered and removed from the official Rust package registry. ##

item.title: Critical Cisco SNMP Flaw Under Active Attack Grants Hackers Root Access to Network Devices
item.dc:creator: ClickControl
item.description: Cisco has issued an urgent alert for CVE-2025-20352, a high-severity vulnerability (CVSS 7.7) in IOS and IOS XE software's SNMP subsystem that's being actively exploited. The flaw allows attackers to cause denial-of-service or execute arbitrary code as root, depending on their privilege level. All Cisco IOS/IOS XE versions with SNMP enabled, Meraki MS390 switches, and Catalyst 9300 Series switches are affected. IT teams must immediately upgrade to IOS XE Release 17.15.4a or later, restrict SNMP access, and review administrator credentials to mitigate this critical security risk.
